sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are active uniformly (`exit_confirm_screens`: 2, `reentry_cooldown_screens`: 1, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp`: 10.0) and are suppressing the worst flip patterns: all three focus tracks show `adjacent_flip_count`: 0, `duplicate_day_skip`: false, and `buffered_holdings`: 0 on the latest run. Cost drag remains uneven—rules at `cost_drag`: 0.2283 and ai_judgment at 0.1613 still trigger watch alerts, while momentum_grace sits at 0.0291 with only 5 lifetime trades—so guards are blocking adjacent-day churn but not enough turnover on the primary and control books. The rules epoch is modestly cleaner (`epoch.cost_drag`: 0.0387, 4 post-epoch trades) than lifetime, and ai_judgment just applied `min_conviction`: 0.2 with a counterfactual hint of `cost_drag_delta`: 0.0872, but that knob epoch has `equity_marks`: 0 and `post_apply_trade_count`: 0, so post-guard improvement is unproven. The single biggest operational learning gap is insufficient post-apply epoch marks on the primary ai_judgment track (`benchmark_span_available`: false, `enough_epoch_history`: false)—we cannot yet tell whether the conviction raise actually lowers churn drag or excess after costs.

sections.proposed_experiments:
1. [paper_churn] Raise `min_rebalance_notional_gbp` from 10.0 to 25.0 on rules and ai_judgment config — both tracks logged 16 trades in 7d with symmetric 8/8 buy-sell churn despite current guards; expected learning value: measure whether notional floor cuts small rebalance legs and lowers 7d `cost_drag` without increasing `adjacent_flip_count`.

2. [paper_churn] Bump rules `exit_confirm_screens` from 2 to 3 (hold `reentry_cooldown_screens`: 1) — rules lifetime `cost_drag`: 0.2283 on 39 trades vs momentum_grace 0.0291 on 5; expected learning value: isolate whether extra exit confirmation screens reduce full_exits (rules logged 8 in 7d) and epoch-scoped drag below 0.0387.

3. [offline_sim] Rules-track lifetime trade replay at `min_conviction`: 0.65–0.70 (mirror ai_judgment counterfactual scope) — ai_judgment replay at 0.2 showed `estimated_cost_savings_gbp`: 87.22; expected learning value: quantify whether a higher conviction floor on the control book would have blocked enough of 22 buys / 17 sells to justify a manual config edit before live cutover.
